'''Ann Catrina Coleman''' (née '''Bryce'''; born 1956) is a Scottish [[electrical engineer]] and professor at the [[University of Texas at Dallas]] specialising in [[semiconductor lasers]]. She is an Associate Vice President (for membership development) of the Photonics Society.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ann Catrina Coleman - Faculty Profiles- Erik Jonsson School of Engineering & Computer Science - The University of Texas at Dallas|url=https://www.utdallas.edu/dept/ee/people/facultypages/Coleman-Ann.html|access-date=2020-09-11|website=www.utdallas.edu|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231109102754/https://www.utdallas.edu/dept/ee/people/facultypages/Coleman-Ann.html|archive-date=9 November 2023|url-status=dead}}</ref> 

== Early life and education ==
{{unreferenced section|date=March 2026}}
Coleman was born in [[Glasgow]], Scotland, in 1956, the first daughter of Nora (McColl) and Vincent Redvers Hanna. She was educated at St. Stephen's Primary School in [[Dalmuir]] and [[Our Lady and St Patrick's High School|Notre Dame High School]] in Dumbarton. She then graduated with a BSc degree in physics from the [[University of Glasgow]] in 1978, and took teacher training at [[St. Andrew's College of Education|St. Andrews College of Education]] in [[Bearsden]]. After two years as a high school physics teacher, she returned to the University of Glasgow and was awarded the PhD in physics in 1987.

== Career ==
After graduating, she remained at the University of Glasgow. She joined the [[Optoelectronics|Optoelectronics Group]] of the Department of Electronics and Electrical Engineering at the University of Glasgow as a postdoctoral [[research assistant]] and was appointed a research fellow in 1992, becoming a senior research fellow in 1997 and professorial research fellow in 2005. She and the other members of this group are primarily recognised for their pioneering work on fabricating [[photonic integrated circuits]] on III-V semiconductor chips based on quantum well intermixing.

In 2012, Coleman joined<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ece.illinois.edu/mediacenter/article.asp?id=1641|title=New faculty member Bryce is an expert in optoelectronics|last=Services|first=Engineering IT Shared|website=ece.illinois.edu|access-date=|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140809150444/https://www.ece.illinois.edu/mediacenter/article.asp?id=1641|archive-date=9 August 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign]] working in the Micro and Nanotechnology Laboratory. In 2013, she moved<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://ece.utdallas.edu/people/facultypages/Coleman-Ann.html|title=Ann Catrina Coleman|website=ece.utdallas.edu|access-date=2017-11-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171211133149/http://ece.utdallas.edu/people/facultypages/Coleman-Ann.html|archive-date=11 December 2017|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref> to the University of Texas at Dallas as professor of electrical engineering and materials science and engineering.

== Honours and professional activities ==
Coleman was elected a fellow of the [[Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers]] in 2008 for contributions to compound semiconductor integrated optoelectronic devices,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ieee.org/membership_services/membership/fellows/women.html |title=Women IEEE Fellows|accessdate=25 August 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110805000352/http://www.ieee.org/membership_services/membership/fellows/women.html |archivedate=5 August 2011|website=IEEE }}</ref> and fellow of the [[Optical Society of America]] in 2009.<ref>[http://www.osa.org/aboutosa/awards/fellows/recentfellows/2009.aspx OSA Awards & Honors] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090319161242/http://www.osa.org/aboutosa/awards/fellows/recentfellows/2009.aspx |date=19 March 2009 }}</ref> In 2006 she shared<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ieee.org/organizations/pubs/newsletters/leos/dec06/profiles_recipients.html|title=LEOS Profiles: 2006 Award Recipients|website=[[IEEE]]|access-date=19 August 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080511235131/http://www.ieee.org/organizations/pubs/newsletters/leos/dec06/profiles_recipients.html|archive-date=11 May 2008|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref> (with J.H. Marsh) the [[IEEE Photonics Society]] (formerly Lasers and Electro-Optics Society) Engineering Achievement Award for extensive development and commercialization of quantum well intermixing for photonic devices.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.photonicssociety.org/awards/engineering-achievement-award/engineering-achievement-award-winners|title=Engineering Achievement Award Winners|website=photonicssociety.org|language=en-gb|access-date=2018-06-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171117122334/https://www.photonicssociety.org/awards/engineering-achievement-award/engineering-achievement-award-winners|archive-date=17 November 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> Coleman has been an elected board member and vice president of the IEEE Photonics Society.<ref>{{Cite journal|date=October 2017|title=Get to Know Your Society Leadership|journal=IEEE Photonics Society News|volume=31|pages=10–11}}</ref> She has published more than 100 papers in scholarly journals with more than 40 invited presentations and publications.
